To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

six novel rearranged cholesterane glycosides were isolated from the plant Ornithogalium saundersiae, and that the cytostatic activities of the isolated compounds on human leukemia HL- 60 cells were investigated.
the rearranged cholestanic glycosides, saundersiosides E, F, and G, with an aromatic acid moiety at the glycosyl moiety, showed high cytostatic activity against human leukemia HL- 60 cells.
six novel rearranged cholestanol derivatives were isolated from the bulb of Ornithogalam saundersiae and the cytostatic activity of the isolated compounds was evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical investigation of Ornithogalu saundersiae and the isolation and characterization of novel cytotoxic cholestane glycolipids.
the isolation and structural elucidation of the rearranged steroid glycosides from Ornithogalums and the evaluation of their cytotoxicity.
the chemical investigation of the bulbs of O. saundersiae, and isolation of the cytostatic compounds, which may be useful as a lead compound for the development of new anticancer agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the aromatic acid ester at the glycosidic moiety is essential for the cytostatic activity of the rearranged glycosidic cholestanes.
these rearranged cholest-5-ene-3,6,7-triol glycosides with an aromatic acid moiety at the glycosyl group would be promising lead compounds for anticancer drug design.
the rearranged cholestanoid glycosides, especially those having an aromatic acid esters group at the glycan moiety, are promising cytostatic agents for human leukemia cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rearranged cholestanic skeleton is an effective scaffold for cytostatic activity.
the aromatic acid esters at the glycosidic side chains are responsible for the high cytostatic activity of the compounds.
the rearranged cholesterols are the key compounds for the cytostatic activity of the bulbs of O. saundersiae.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rearranged cholestanol glycosides isolated from the bulbs are cytostatic to HL-60 cells with an IC50 value of 0.01-0.05 microM, which is comparable to that of the clinically applied antitumor drugs, etoposid, methotrexate and doxorubicin.
rearranged sterol glycosides with an aromatic acid moiety at the glycosidic moiety are highly cytostatic, which is a new finding for sterol glycoside derivatives.
rearranged cholest-5-ene glycosides with an aromatic acid residue at the glycosidic moiety are promising candidates for the development of anticancer agents.
